claims.statement: The role directives are Markdown files embedded into the mc binary with go:embed, one per role plus collie.md.
directiveForRole appends a generated skill pointer to the directive prose rather than inlining skill bodies.
The Strategist command pointer requires the installed mc-strategist skill before each mc call and states that mc has no help command.
An unknown role has no fallback directive; roleProseDirective returns an error.
The run brief format is mc.spawn-brief.v23.
The Scribe brief identifies its Project, accepted start commit, and prior successful start commit when available.
renderRunBrief writes a header with the schema version, the role directive inside role_directive tags, then each part as a heading, an explanation, and facts, tagged text, or a JSON block.
Only the Strategist and the Arbiter receive the Vision part.
RoleSkillSet orders a role's skills as the command surface, then additional skills, then shared skills, and skillByPath requires the frontmatter name to equal the directory name.
composeRunSkills appends operator skills after the shipped set and refuses an operator skill that takes a shipped name.
installRunSkills replaces the skill root within the container's separate role storage.
TestRunBriefExplainsEachPart requires unique part headings and an explanation of one or two sentences ending in a period.
AGENTS.md requires a change to what a role does, receives, or can call to update the role directive, run brief explanations, and skills without holding history.
Setup operations receive a separate brief with the setup directive, assigned environment facts, retained configuration, setup skills, and continuation requirements.
The setup directive requires an ordered checklist that assesses every missing prerequisite before the final image decision.
The shared environment skill requires material development benefit and credible feasibility evidence for image proposals, within each role's authority.
The setup agent input test checks prerequisite assessment, permitted probes, uncertainty, continuation requirements, and inclusion of setup skills.
Setup and pipeline agents share execution permissions and limits while role authority and credentials remain separate.
The Strategist operator skill directory remains strategist-propose while its shipped command skill uses strategist/mc-strategist/SKILL.md.
The run brief title identifies the role as Strategist.
The Collie runner requests packet context for a turn without a native session reference and checks the session, packet, and version identifiers.
The Collie directive requires current packet reads for mutable state and decisions, and explicit confirmation before a new state change.
The shared environment skill requires fresh source and repeated dependency preparation against the persistent Project home, with Scribe, Strategist, and Arbiter exemptions.
Each Worker run on revised requirements receives the revision reason as context; Verifier and Packager briefs omit that reason.
The Verifier requires an operator decision when a criterion check or new or changed test needs a capability that no agent container has.
The Strategist directive requires each success criterion to name a check that the Worker and Verifier can run in an agent container.
The Arbiter directive requires container-checkable proposal criteria and excludes host access, a Docker daemon, macOS interfaces, additional privileges, and hosted CI runs.
Proposal briefs select up to 10 cancelled tasks, then rejected tasks within a total limit of 20, ordered by decision time and identifier.
Historical entries omit descriptions and include a normalized cancellation reason excerpt of at most 160 Unicode characters when available.
The history tests cover limits, Project isolation, decision order, cancellation excerpts, source reason preservation, and complete active context.
The dispatch protocol retains DedupeTitles while the brief selects historical tasks from the spine snapshot.
The Packager brief, directive, and command skill identify the dashboard as the page style owner; the directive and skill require preservation of that style.
The Collie command skill directs Discord configuration to Configs → Discord and states that setup codes grant no agent authority.
The Worker directive requires preservation of the supplied connection configuration and exclusion of Culler tokens from output.
The Strategist and Arbiter directives prohibit whole-suite success criteria.
The Worker input requires successful new or changed tests and correction of task regressions.
The Verifier input requires broad checks and base comparisons for submitted failures.
The Packager input preserves unchanged failures and unverified coverage without an additional approval requirement.
The Collie directive and skill describe a Discord thread and the dashboard as two surfaces of one Collie session.
The Verifier, Packager, and setup directives identify the profile as the source of model and effort.
The private runtime binding carries profile effort into the launch capability.
The Scribe skills require page-specific source review, Claim inspection, original document preservation, and recovery from unavailable history.
The Worker and Verifier command pointers supply a failure terminal when the command skill is absent or unreadable.
The Verifier contract includes Assessment duties and the unavailable-check outcomes, which Project customization must preserve.
Worker and Verifier briefs omit credentials, failure controls, correction allowances, and the correction count while retaining assignment and case data.
The platform input tests check unavailable-check procedures, the failed-read fallback, independent checks, and retention of unverified evidence.
The Strategist brief omits Agent credentials and Failure controls while retaining assignment data and concise explanations.
The Strategist directive points to execution, operator decision, and customization procedures; the command skill also supplies the dependency procedure.
The Strategist input tests check selected rules once across the rendered brief and command skill, with shared skill contents excluded.
The Strategist directive requires evidence for a useful result, checks existing capabilities, and considers effort and risk before proposal submission.
The rendered Strategist brief test checks task selection guidance and customization boundaries.
The Strategist directive requires two proposals together; its command skill permits an empty batch when no valid task remains.
The Arbiter directive points to conditional procedures for historical work, all-reject batches, dependencies, execution problems, and operator decisions.
The Arbiter command pointer requires the installed mc-arbiter skill before the first command and before the terminal.
The Arbiter brief omits Agent credentials and Failure controls while preserving assignment payloads and relevant operator resolutions.
The Arbiter input test checks selected rules once across the rendered brief and command skill and excludes shared skill contents.
The Arbiter audit uses whitespace-separated token counts and records a directive reduction from 2029 to 545 and a skill reduction from 1576 to 612.
The Arbiter audit records passing changed tests and an unchanged operator-home failure in the full mc check, with host checks left unverified.
